newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir leader gives rebels 30 days to surrender.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir leader gives rebels 30 days to surrender.

text.p: Kashmir Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah urged separatist militants on Saturday to surrender their weapons in 30 days, or face a crackdown by Indian security forces.
"I give them 30 days to surrender their weapons before any government official," Abdullah told a news conference in the summer capital of Srinagar. "I have decided to get them in the mainstream."

Abdullah did not say if he would call a ceasefire during the period between the security forces and militant groups who have been fighting Indian rule in the Himalayan state since 1990. He said at least 50,000 people have been killed in the separatist violence.

"If they don't surrender, they will face further guns," Abdullah said. He also warned Kashmir's recently raised pro-government militias to surrender their guns, promising them jobs in Indian security units.
Abdullah, the leader of Kashmir's National Conference party, won an absolute majority in the state assembly last month when India held the first elections there in nine years.
In a tearful speech during his inauguration earlier this month, Abdullah said: "The last drop of my blood is dedicated to India."
